items.title: Symmetric-power SU2 representation

references.title: MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 2 'Spin one-half, Bras, Kets, and Operators' (spin-half systems and their operators) and Chapter 9 'Angular Momentum', §2 pp. 11-18 (Commuting observables; algebraic theory of angular momentum)
J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Chapter 7 (Angular Momentum), §7.1 pp. 141-152 (rotation operators and ladder algebra) and §7.4.2 pp. 161-164 (spin-half matrices)
MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 8 'Multiparticle States and Tensor Products' (tensor products and product bases)

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix an integer $n\ge1$, let
$V:=\mathbb C^2$ carry the standard inner product linear in the first argument, with orthonormal basis
$(e_+,e_-)$ where $e_+:=(1,0)$ and $e_-:=(0,1)$ ([[def-inner-product-space]]), and let $V^{\otimes n}$ be the
$n$-fold tensor power with the inner product of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]] and place permutations $U_\pi$ ($\pi$ in the symmetric group
$S_n$, [[def-finite-symmetric-group-and-permutation-notation]]) of
[[def-commuting-symmetric-and-linear-actions-on-tensor-power]], with the diagonal action $W^{\otimes n}$ of
$W\in M_2(\mathbb C)$ and the operators
$\Delta(T):=\sum_{j=1}^{n}\mathbf 1^{\otimes(j-1)}\otimes T\otimes\mathbf 1^{\otimes(n-j)}$. Put

$$P_+:=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}U_\pi,\qquad \mathcal S_n:=\operatorname{ran}P_+\subseteq V^{\otimes n},\qquad SU(2):=\{W\in M_2(\mathbb C): W^*W=I_2,\ \det W=1\},$$

where $W^*:=\overline W^{\mathsf T}$ is the conjugate transpose of $W$ and $I_2$ the identity matrix
([[def-matrix-product-and-identity-matrix]], [[def-determinant-of-a-square-matrix]]). For $W\in SU(2)$ define
$U_n(W):=W^{\otimes n}|_{\mathcal S_n}$. For $k\in\{0,\dots,n\}$ let $s_k$ be the sum of the elementary tensors
$e_{\varepsilon_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{\varepsilon_n}$ over all $2^n$ strings
$(\varepsilon_1,\dots,\varepsilon_n)\in\{+,-\}^n$ containing exactly $k$ entries $-$, and put
$v_k:=\binom nk^{-1/2}s_k$.

Then:

(a) $P_+$ is the orthogonal projection onto the closed subspace $\mathcal S_n$, $U_\pi$ and $W^{\otimes n}$ commute for
every $\pi\in S_n$ and every $W$, and $W^{\otimes n}(\mathcal S_n)\subseteq \mathcal S_n$; the assignment $W\mapsto U_n(W)$ is
well defined on all of $M_2(\mathbb C)$, and $U_n(W')U_n(W)=U_n(W'W)$ holds for all $W,W'$;

(b) $SU(2)$ is a subgroup of the multiplicative monoid of $M_2(\mathbb C)$ with identity $I_2$; for $W\in SU(2)$
the operator $U_n(W)$ is unitary with inverse $U_n(W^{-1})=U_n(W)^*$, so $U_n:SU(2)\to U(\mathcal S_n)$ is a group
homomorphism ([[def-strongly-continuous-unitary-representation]],
[[def-linear-isometry-and-orthogonal-or-unitary-operator]]);

(c) the vectors $v_0,\dots,v_n$ form an orthonormal basis of $\mathcal S_n$; in particular $\mathcal S_n$ is $(n+1)$-dimensional;

(d) the operators $J_i:=\tfrac12\Delta(\sigma_i)|_{\mathcal S_n}$, $i=x,y,z$, where $\sigma_x,\sigma_y,\sigma_z$ are the
Pauli matrices of [[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]], are self-adjoint and satisfy, with
$J_\pm:=J_x\pm iJ_y$, $J^2:=J_x^2+J_y^2+J_z^2$,

$$J_zv_k=\bigl(\tfrac n2-k\bigr)v_k,\qquad J_+v_k=\sqrt{k(n-k+1)}\,v_{k-1},\qquad J_-v_k=\sqrt{(k+1)(n-k)}\,v_{k+1},$$

with $v_{-1}:=0$ and $v_{n+1}:=0$; moreover $[J_z,J_\pm]=\pm J_\pm$, $[J_+,J_-]=2J_z$,
$[J_i,J_j]=i\sum_k\varepsilon_{ijk}J_k$ and $J^2=\tfrac n2\bigl(\tfrac n2+1\bigr)I_{\mathcal S_n}$; the map
$v_k\mapsto e_{n/2-k}$ is a unitary equivalence of $(J_x,J_y,J_z)$ with the spin-$\tfrac n2$ matrices of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]];

(e) for each $i$ the curve $A_i(t):=\cos(t/2)I_2-i\sin(t/2)\sigma_i$ ($t\in\mathbb R$) lies in $SU(2)$, satisfies
$A_i(s)A_i(t)=A_i(s+t)$ and $A_i'(0)=-\tfrac i2\sigma_i$, and $t\mapsto V_i(t):=U_n(A_i(t))$ is a strongly
continuous one-parameter unitary group on $\mathcal S_n$ ([[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]])
whose infinitesimal generator $G_i$ ([[def-infinitesimal-generator-of-a-unitary-group]]) is $G_i=-iJ_i$ on all
of $\mathcal S_n$; equivalently $\frac1t\bigl(V_i(t)v-v\bigr)\to-iJ_iv$ for every $v\in \mathcal S_n$;

(f) $U_n$ is strongly continuous on $SU(2)$: if $W_m\to W_0$ in $M_2(\mathbb C)$ with all $W_m\in SU(2)$ and
$W_0\in SU(2)$, then $\|U_n(W_m)-U_n(W_0)\|\to0$ in the operator norm on $\mathcal S_n$.

This is finite-dimensional linear algebra: the theorem constructs a unitary representation of $SU(2)$ and its
generators. It does not assert that $SU(2)$ or any spin observable describes a physical particle, and it makes
no measurement or statistics claim.

items.title: Tensor spin composition

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Chapter 7 (Angular Momentum), §7.5 pp. 173-176 (addition of angular momenta) and §7.5.1 pp. 173-175 (case j1 = j2 = 1/2)

MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 9 'Angular Momentum', §2 pp. 11-18 (algebraic theory and weights) and Chapter 8 'Multiparticle States and Tensor Products' (tensor products and product bases)

items.statement:
Let $s,t\in\frac12\mathbb N$, write $L_s:=\{-s,-s+1,\dots,s\}$ and $L_t:=\{-t,-t+1,\dots,t\}$, and let
$(V_s,J^{(s)}_x,J^{(s)}_y,J^{(s)}_z)$ and $(V_t,J^{(t)}_x,J^{(t)}_y,J^{(t)}_z)$ be the spin models of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] with orthonormal bases $(e^{(s)}_m)_{m\in L_s}$ and
$(e^{(t)}_n)_{n\in L_t}$ and the ladders $J^{(s)}_\pm:=J^{(s)}_x\pm iJ^{(s)}_y$,
$J^{(t)}_\pm:=J^{(t)}_x\pm iJ^{(t)}_y$ and Casimirs $J^{(s)2}$, $J^{(t)2}$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]). On the tensor product $V_s\otimes V_t$ put

$$J^{\mathrm{tot}}_i:=J^{(s)}_i\otimes I_{V_t}+I_{V_s}\otimes J^{(t)}_i\quad(i=x,y,z),\qquad J^{\mathrm{tot}}_\pm:=J^{\mathrm{tot}}_x\pm iJ^{\mathrm{tot}}_y,\qquad J^{\mathrm{tot}\,2}:=(J^{\mathrm{tot}}_x)^2+(J^{\mathrm{tot}}_y)^2+(J^{\mathrm{tot}}_z)^2 .$$

Then:

(a) each $J^{\mathrm{tot}}_i$ is self-adjoint, the triple $J^{\mathrm{tot}}_x,J^{\mathrm{tot}}_y,J^{\mathrm{tot}}_z$
satisfies the commutation relations of
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-block-decomposition]], and
$J^{\mathrm{tot}\,2}=J^{(s)2}\otimes I_{V_t}+I_{V_s}\otimes J^{(t)2}+2\sum_{i}J^{(s)}_i\otimes J^{(t)}_i$ is
self-adjoint and commutes with $J^{\mathrm{tot}}_x,J^{\mathrm{tot}}_y,J^{\mathrm{tot}}_z$;

(b) there is an orthogonal decomposition $V_s\otimes V_t=\bigoplus_{j=|s-t|}^{s+t}W_j$ into
$J^{\mathrm{tot}}$-invariant subspaces, one for each $j\in\{|s-t|,|s-t|+1,\dots,s+t\}$, with
$\dim W_j=2j+1$, on each of which $(J^{\mathrm{tot}}_x,J^{\mathrm{tot}}_y,J^{\mathrm{tot}}_z)$ is unitarily
equivalent to the spin-$j$ model of [[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]]; consequently
$\sum_{j=|s-t|}^{s+t}(2j+1)=(2s+1)(2t+1)$;

(c) for every $M\in\frac12\mathbb Z$ the $M$-eigenspace of $J^{\mathrm{tot}}_z$ has dimension
$$N(M):=\#\{m\in L_s:\ M-m\in L_t\}=\begin{cases}\max\bigl(0,\ \min(s,M+t)-\max(-s,M-t)+1\bigr),&M-(s+t)\in\mathbb Z,\\0,&M-(s+t)\notin\mathbb Z.\end{cases},$$
and the identity $(e^{(s)}_m\otimes e^{(t)}_n)_{m,n}$ is an orthonormal basis of $V_s\otimes V_t$ consisting of
eigenvectors of $J^{\mathrm{tot}}_z$ with eigenvalues $m+n$;

(d) the number of summands with parameter equal to $M$ in the decomposition of (b) is
$N(M)-N(M+1)$ if $M\ge0$, and this number equals $1$ when $M-(s+t)\in\mathbb Z$ and $|s-t|\le M\le s+t$, and equals $0$ otherwise; hence the
multiset of parameters in (b) is exactly $\{|s-t|,|s-t|+1,\dots,s+t\}$, each occurring once;

(e) for each $j\in\{|s-t|,\dots,s+t\}$ the space of vectors of $J^{\mathrm{tot}}_z$-eigenvalue $j$ orthogonal to
all summands $W_{j'}$ with $j'>j$ is one-dimensional; for a unit vector $u_j$ in it the vectors
$$v_{j,k}:=\bigl(k!(2j)(2j-1)\cdots(2j-k+1)\bigr)^{-1/2}(J^{\mathrm{tot}}_-)^ku_j\qquad(0\le k\le2j)$$
form an orthonormal basis of $W_j$ with $J^{\mathrm{tot}}_zv_{j,k}=(j-k)v_{j,k}$,
$J^{\mathrm{tot}}_+v_{j,k}=\sqrt{k(2j-k+1)}\,v_{j,k-1}$ and
$J^{\mathrm{tot}}_-v_{j,k}=\sqrt{(k+1)(2j-k)}\,v_{j,k+1}$; the coefficients of $v_{j,k}$ in the product basis
are therefore determined by the phase of $u_j$, and choosing that phase fixes the Clebsch-Gordan numbers
explicitly; in particular $u_{s+t}=e^{(s)}_s\otimes e^{(t)}_t$ is a permissible choice.

The theorem is a purely mathematical statement about tensor products of the explicit matrices of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]]; it asserts no physical coupling, conservation law or
measurement fact.

items.title: Tsirelson bound

references.title: N. Brunner, D. Cavalcanti, S. Pironio, V. Scarani, S. Wehner, 'Bell nonlocality', Reviews of Modern Physics 86 (2014) 419, Section II.C.1.a (equation (31) and the operator identity S^2 = 4 + [A1,A2][B1,B2], giving ||S|| <= 2 sqrt 2) and Section II (CHSH inequality (4) and the classical bound S <= 2)

L. J. Landau, 'On the violation of Bell's inequality in quantum theory', Physics Letters A 120 (1987) 54-56 (operator derivation of the CHSH quantum bound), as reported and used in the review above; the operator square identity used here is verified directly in the proof

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,K$ be complex Hilbert spaces
([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let $A_0,A_1\in\mathcal B(H)$, $B_0,B_1\in\mathcal B(K)$ be bounded self-adjoint
operators ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]) with
$A_i^2=I_H$ and $B_j^2=I_K$ ([[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]]). Let $H\widehat\otimes K$ be the completed tensor
product of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]] and put

$$C:=A_0\otimes(B_0+B_1)+A_1\otimes(B_0-B_1)\in\mathcal B(H\widehat\otimes K).$$

Then:

(a) $C$ is self-adjoint and
$$C^2=4\,I_{H\widehat\otimes K}-[A_0,A_1]\otimes[B_0,B_1];$$

(b) $\|C^2\|\le8$ and $\|C\|\le2\sqrt2$ in the operator norm
([[def-operator-norm]], [[thm-hilbert-adjoint-properties]]);

(c) for all $\psi,\psi'\in H\widehat\otimes K$, $|\langle C\psi,\psi'\rangle|\le2\sqrt2\,\|\psi\|\,\|\psi'\|$
(this is the Tsirelson bound for the stated pair of binary sharp models); consequently the absolute value of the
CHSH combination of the four expectations $\langle(A_i\otimes B_j)\psi,\psi\rangle$ of a unit vector $\psi$ is at
most $2\sqrt2$;

(d) the bound is attained on $H=K=\mathbb C^2$: let $\sigma_x,\sigma_y,\sigma_z$ be the Pauli matrices of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]], let
$\Psi:=\frac1{\sqrt2}(e_+\otimes e_--e_-\otimes e_+)$ with the orthonormal basis $(e_+,e_-)$ of $\mathbb C^2$, put
$\sigma_a:=a_x\sigma_x+a_y\sigma_y+a_z\sigma_z$ for a unit vector $a\in\mathbb R^3$, and take
$A_0:=\sigma_z$, $A_1:=\sigma_x$, $B_0:=\sigma_{(z+x)/\sqrt2}$, $B_1:=\sigma_{(z-x)/\sqrt2}$; then
$\langle\sigma_a\otimes\sigma_b\Psi,\Psi\rangle=-a\cdot b$ for all unit $a,b$, and
$\langle C\Psi,\Psi\rangle=-2\sqrt2$, so $|\langle C\Psi,\Psi\rangle|=2\sqrt2$;

(e) a comparison with the stated local model: if in addition $A_0,A_1,B_0,B_1$ are four $\pm1$-valued random
variables on one probability space, then the absolute value of their CHSH combination is at most $2$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-chsh-and-finite-sampling-law]] (a)); this is a statement about that explicitly specified
common-outcome model, not about all theories, and it is not compared here with any reported experiment.

The theorem is a mathematical statement about bounded operators; no measurement, preparation or empirical claim
is asserted.

title: Qm Math Orbital And Spin — Examples

items.title: Spin singlet CHSH

references.title: N. Brunner, D. Cavalcanti, S. Pironio, V. Scarani and S. Wehner, 'Bell nonlocality', Reviews of Modern Physics 86 (2014), §II.C.1.a (CHSH inequality and the singlet correlations E = -a.b) and eq. (4)
J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Chapter 6 (the singlet state of two spin-half particles) and Chapter 7 (Pauli operators)

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $V=\mathbb C^2$ carry the orthonormal basis
$(e_+,e_-)$ and let $\sigma_x,\sigma_y,\sigma_z$ be the Pauli matrices of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] (e), with $\sigma_a:=\sum_{i\in\{x,y,z\}}a_i\sigma_i$
for $a\in\mathbb R^3$; on the completed tensor product $V\widehat\otimes V$ use the inner product of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]. Define the **singlet vector**
$$\Psi:=\frac1{\sqrt2}\bigl(e_+\otimes e_--e_-\otimes e_+\bigr)\in V\widehat\otimes V .$$
Then:

(a) $\|\Psi\|=1$ and $\langle(\sigma_i\otimes\sigma_j)\Psi,\Psi\rangle=-\delta_{ij}$ for all
$i,j\in\{x,y,z\}$;

(b) for all unit vectors $a,b\in\mathbb R^3$ the **singlet correlation** is
$$\langle(\sigma_a\otimes\sigma_b)\Psi,\Psi\rangle=-a\cdot b;$$

(c) with the unit vectors $a_0:=(1,0,0)$, $a_1:=(0,1,0)$, $b_0:=(1,1,0)/\sqrt2$, $b_1:=(1,-1,0)/\sqrt2$ the
CHSH combination of the four correlations
$$E_{ij}:=\langle(\sigma_{a_i}\otimes\sigma_{b_j})\Psi,\Psi\rangle$$
satisfies
$$E_{00}+E_{01}+E_{10}-E_{11}=-2\sqrt2,\qquad\text{so}\qquad \bigl|E_{00}+E_{01}+E_{10}-E_{11}\bigr|=2\sqrt2,$$
which is the value of the Tsirelson bound of [[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-tsirelson-bound]] (b),(c); thus the bound
is attained at these settings;

(d) since $2\sqrt2>2$, the four numbers $E_{ij}$ of (c) cannot be realized as
$\mathbb E[A_iB_j]$ for four $\pm1$-valued random variables $A_0,A_1,B_0,B_1$ on one probability space, by the
CHSH inequality for that common-outcome model ([[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-tsirelson-bound]] (e)).

All claims are finite-dimensional linear-algebra statements about the indicated matrices and vectors; no
preparation, measurement or experimental claim is made.

items.title: Coupled triplet and singlet

references.title: MIT 8.05 Quantum Physics II (Fall 2013), Chapter 8 'Tensor product' (addition of angular momenta; the 1/2 x 1/2 example with triplet and singlet)
J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Chapter 7, §7.4.2 (addition of angular momenta and the two spin-half example)

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $V=\mathbb C^2$ carry the orthonormal basis
$(e_+,e_-)$ and let $(J^{(1/2)}_x,J^{(1/2)}_y,J^{(1/2)}_z)$ be the spin-$\tfrac12$ operators of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]], so that $J^{(1/2)}_i=\tfrac12\sigma_i$ and
$J^{(1/2)}_\pm=J^{(1/2)}_x\pm iJ^{(1/2)}_y$ satisfy $J^{(1/2)}_+e_+=0$, $J^{(1/2)}_+e_-=e_+$,
$J^{(1/2)}_-e_+=e_-$ and $J^{(1/2)}_-e_-=0$. On $V\widehat\otimes V$ (inner product of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]) put, as in
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-tensor-spin-composition]],
$$J^{\mathrm{tot}}_i:=J^{(1/2)}_i\otimes I_2+I_2\otimes J^{(1/2)}_i,\qquad J^{\mathrm{tot}}_\pm:=J^{\mathrm{tot}}_x\pm iJ^{\mathrm{tot}}_y,\qquad J^{\mathrm{tot}\,2}:=(J^{\mathrm{tot}}_x)^2+(J^{\mathrm{tot}}_y)^2+(J^{\mathrm{tot}}_z)^2,$$
and define
$$w_{1,1}:=e_+\otimes e_+,\quad w_{1,0}:=\frac{e_+\otimes e_-+e_-\otimes e_+}{\sqrt2},\quad w_{1,-1}:=e_-\otimes e_-,\quad w_{0,0}:=\frac{e_+\otimes e_--e_-\otimes e_+}{\sqrt2}.$$
Then:

(a) $(w_{1,1},w_{1,0},w_{1,-1},w_{0,0})$ is an orthonormal basis of $V\widehat\otimes V$;

(b) the triplet vectors satisfy $J^{\mathrm{tot}}_zw_{1,m}=m\,w_{1,m}$ and $J^{\mathrm{tot}\,2}w_{1,m}=2\,w_{1,m}$
for $m\in\{1,0,-1\}$, while the singlet satisfies $J^{\mathrm{tot}}_iw_{0,0}=0$ for each $i\in\{x,y,z\}$ and
$J^{\mathrm{tot}\,2}w_{0,0}=0$;

(c) the ladder actions on the triplet are $J^{\mathrm{tot}}_+w_{1,1}=0$, $J^{\mathrm{tot}}_+w_{1,0}=\sqrt2\,w_{1,1}$
and $J^{\mathrm{tot}}_+w_{1,-1}=\sqrt2\,w_{1,0}$, together with the adjoint relations
$J^{\mathrm{tot}}_-w_{1,-1}=0$, $J^{\mathrm{tot}}_-w_{1,0}=\sqrt2\,w_{1,-1}$ and
$J^{\mathrm{tot}}_-w_{1,1}=\sqrt2\,w_{1,0}$; hence the correspondence $e_m\leftrightarrow w_{1,m}$ is a unitary
isomorphism of the spin-$1$ model of [[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]] onto the triplet span,
so the orthogonal decomposition of
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-tensor-spin-composition]] (b) is here
$V\widehat\otimes V=\operatorname{span}\{w_{1,1},w_{1,0},w_{1,-1}\}\oplus\operatorname{span}\{w_{0,0}\}$
with parameters $j=1$ and $j=0$ and dimensions $3+1=4$, summing to $(2\cdot\tfrac12+1)^2$.

All claims are finite-dimensional linear-algebra statements; no physical interpretation of the vectors as particle
states is asserted.
items.strategy: Complete finite verification of the $1/2\otimes1/2$ Clebsch-Gordan basis; see the numbered steps in the item body.
